surface: Line-restriction derivative in the Wolfe curvature condition
source_issue: The source states phi prime at delta k equals the gradient evaluated at x k dotted with p k; that right-hand side is only phi prime at zero and drops the shifted evaluation point.
target_action: Applied the chain rule with the gradient evaluated at x k plus delta p k and retained the correct ascent-form curvature inequality phi prime at delta k at most sigma 2 phi prime at zero.

surface: Two-dimensional line restriction and accepted curvature region
source_issue: The source inserts the full gradient vector separately into both scalar coordinates of f and later says the curvature condition accepts derivatives greater than a constant although the displayed inequality accepts derivatives no greater than sigma 2 phi prime at zero.
target_action: Defined the path vectorially as x zero plus t times the gradient, described the accepted derivative region with the displayed inequality, and limited the bracketing interpretation to the illustrated example.

surface: Existence of Wolfe steps and finite termination of Armijo backtracking
source_issue: The lemma uses continuous differentiability without stating it and says merely bounded where bounded above is required; the backtracking termination claim is attributed to the stronger Wolfe lemma rather than the local derivative argument actually sufficient for Armijo.
target_action: Stated C1 regularity and boundedness above on the ray, completed the open-neighborhood conclusion for both strict inequalities, and justified finite Armijo backtracking directly from phi prime at zero being positive.

source_issue: The reader delegates its algorithm to a Maple listing whose component rights are unclear or external and whose input contract does not reject beta equal to zero or one.
target_action: Excluded the Maple component and supplied independently authored locale-neutral pseudocode with explicit domains for t zero, beta, sigma one, the ascent derivative, the shrink loop, and the returned step; no Maple syntax or implementation text was copied.

source_issue: The theorem assumes only that a step satisfies Armijo, which permits summable arbitrarily small steps converging to a nonstationary point, while its proof silently uses the rejected predecessor property of backtracking, upgrades a limsup to a full-subsequence lower bound, and preserves a strict inequality after taking a limit.
target_action: Required fixed-parameter backtracking, selected a subsequence on which directional derivatives have a positive uniform lower bound, used the rejected predecessor step and a convergent direction subsequence, and took the limit with a non-strict inequality that still contradicts the positive lower bound and sigma one less than one.

surface: Exact-search and positive-definite scaling corollaries and their exercises
source_issue: The source asserts unconditional convergence for exact line search without requiring finite maximizers or convergence of the generated iterates, pointwise positive definiteness of varying B k alone does not make the directions gradient related, and the exact-search exercise switches from the defined Armijo parameter sigma one to an undefined sigma.
target_action: Required existence of each finite exact line maximizer and convergence before concluding stationarity, imposed uniform spectral bounds m I at most B k at most M I together with backtracking and iterate convergence for the scaled-gradient corollary, and restored sigma one in the exercise inequality.

source_issue: The source calls delta k equal to one a decreasing step length and labels a closed-form expression indexed by n as x sub k plus one, obscuring which subsequences approach minus one and plus one.
target_action: Described the step as constant, wrote the closed form for x sub n, and explicitly identified the even and odd subsequential limits.

source_issue: The editable v1.0 source omits the closing norm delimiters in the bound on p k, leaving the mathematical expression malformed; the public v1.0.1 PDF is the frozen correction witness for this exact defect.
target_action: Restored the complete inequality norm p k at most c times norm gradient f at x k while leaving the authority source unchanged.

surface: Quadratic steepest-ascent convergence factor and proof algebra
source_issue: The source calls the ratio of eigenvalue differences to sums the condition number, reverses the slow-convergence interpretation of the actual spectral condition number, claims a strictly positive residual factor even in the one-step eigenvector case, and expands the numerator with lambda 2 instead of lambda n.
target_action: Named the ratio rho as the convergence factor, defined the conventional spectral condition number kappa and rho equals kappa minus one over kappa plus one, allowed a zero residual factor, invoked Cauchy-Schwarz for that endpoint, and corrected the expansion to lambda one squared minus two lambda one lambda n plus lambda n squared.

source_issue: The reader splits an executable implementation across two Maple listing files whose component rights are unclear or external and whose line-search dependency is not a closed open implementation.
target_action: Preserved both algorithm surfaces and their identifier but replaced the excluded listings with independently authored two-part locale-neutral pseudocode exposing inputs, gradient updates, line-search contract, stopping test, returned path, and failure-contract caveat; no Maple code was copied.

surface: Quadratic example matrix and conditioning interpretation
source_issue: For F of x y equal to minus two x squared minus ten y squared, the representation one half x transpose Q x requires Q diagonal minus four and minus twenty, not minus two and minus ten; the source also calls two thirds the condition number.
target_action: Used Q diagonal minus four and minus twenty, reported spectral condition number five, and separately reported the convergence factor two thirds that governs the illustrated zig-zag behavior.

surface: Superlinear convergence theorem and eventual unit-step proof
source_issue: The explanatory remark omits the gradient from the Newton direction and evaluates only a bare inverse Hessian at the limit; the proof replaces a convergent Hessian by an informal similarity sign and hides error terms without establishing uniform positivity over the varying unit directions.
target_action: Stated the Newton direction as minus the current inverse Hessian times the current gradient, decomposed normalized directions using the inverse limit Hessian, controlled all remainder terms uniformly, used negative definiteness to obtain a fixed positive lower bound, and retained the original little-o argument for superlinear convergence.

source_issue: Labels for the gradient-related definition, the general convergence theorem, Kantorovich lemma, gradient-ascent theorem, gradient-ascent example, and superlinear theorem occur after nested numbered equations or a figure caption and can therefore bind to the nested counter instead of the owning environment.
target_action: Kept every identifier unchanged but moved each label immediately after its owning environment opens and before any nested counter-changing content.
